records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration interpolates each migrated host value directly into a SQL string literal. A previously-saved embeddable_hosts entry containing a single quote (the old setting was free-text, e.g. `o'brien.example.com`) terminates the string literal and makes the INSERT raise a PostgreSQL syntax error, aborting db:migrate; it is also a raw SQL injection vector in the migration.
records.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL by interpolating each host string directly into a single-quoted literal: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ... )"`. If `h` contains a single quote (e.g. `o'brien.example.com`) it will terminate the SQL string and cause a syntax error, aborting the migration; since it is unescaped interpolation, it is also a SQL injection vector within the migration.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration uses `create_table ... force: true` and embeds data-migration SQL inside a non-reversible `change` block. `force: true` drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table without warning (destroying data if one exists), and the destructive `DELETE FROM site_settings` plus INSERTs make `rake db:rollback` fail with IrreversibleMigration, leaving no downgrade path for an operator who needs to revert this feature.
records.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which will drop an existing `embeddable_hosts` table if present (data loss risk). It also performs irreversible data changes inside a `change` method via raw SQL `execute` (INSERTs) and `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`; Rails cannot auto-reverse these, so `db:rollback` would raise an irreversible migration error and provides no downgrade path.

records.rationale: The diff removes the previous gating condition in `Topic#expandable_first_post?`. Therefore, when `embed_truncate` is enabled and a topic has an embed, the method can now return true even if there are zero `EmbeddableHost` rows configured, matching the finding’s described regression.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Host values from the old setting are interpolated unescaped into the INSERT, so any value containing a quote or backslash breaks or corrupts the backfill. An admin whose embeddable_hosts setting contained a stray quote or odd hostname (the old free-text setting accepted anything) makes the generated INSERT a SQL syntax error or malformed row, aborting db:migrate after the table create but before site_settings cleanup — leaving the site in a half-migrated state with old settings still present and code already reading only the new table.
records.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL by interpolating each host string directly into a single-quoted literal: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ... )"`. If `h` contains a single quote (e.g. `o'brien.example.com`) it will terminate the SQL string and cause a syntax error, aborting the migration; since it is unescaped interpolation, it is also a SQL injection vector within the migration.

records.issue_text: [BUG] update and destroy call methods on a possibly-nil record (`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`), so a missing or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 where the admin API contract expects a 4xx/404. An admin editing two browser tabs who deletes a host in one and saves it in the other gets a raw 500 (nil.host= / nil.destroy), and the client's catch shows a generic popup instead of a meaningful 'not found'.
records.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch with `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally use `host`. `update` calls `save_host(host)` where `save_host` does `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...`, and `destroy` does `host.destroy`. If no record matches `params[:id]`, `host` is `nil` and these lines will raise `NoMethodError`, yielding a 500 instead of a not-found response.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The delete action calls `destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, so a failed DELETE (server error or network) is an unhandled rejection and the row is never removed but no error is shown to the admin. Admin clicks delete, confirms, sees the row still present with no explanation; the failure is invisible — contrast with save() which correctly uses popupAjaxError.
records.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action does `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); });` with no `.catch(...)`. On DELETE failure, the promise rejection is unhandled and `deleteHost` is never sent, so the row remains and no error is shown. This contrasts with `save()` which explicitly `.catch(popupAjaxError)`.

records.issue_text: [BUG] After a successful save, `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` is called with whatever the category-chooser holds; the server coerces a blank category_id to the uncategorized category while the client looks up the raw (blank/null) id, desynchronizing displayed state from persisted state. Admin who clears the category sees a blank/undefined category badge in the table while the server actually stored uncategorized_category_id — the UI misrepresents what was saved until reload.
records.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, after save the client forces `host.category` from the raw chooser value: `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` even if `categoryId` is blank/null. But on the server, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` explicitly coerces a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` (`host.category_id = ... if host.category_id.blank?`). This can desync the displayed category (blank/undefined badge) from what was persisted (uncategorized) until reload.

Any client sending a create/update without the embeddable_host envelope (e.g. an out-of-date admin bundle after a rolling deploy) gets a raw 500 instead of a 400/422 error.

If a request omits `:embeddable_host`, `params[:embeddable_host]` will be nil and this will raise (NoMethodError), resulting in a 500 rather than a controlled 4xx/validation response.
